findings.finding: The plan explicitly states the provider_factory / infer_model hook was 'verified against pydantic-ai 1.107.1' (cited in providers.py). pydantic-ai v2.0 went stable on June 23 2026 and is now at v2.20.0 with breaking changes. While the infer_model(provider_factory=...) signature does appear to survive in v2's public API (confirmed on ai.pydantic.dev), the plan makes no assertion about v2 compatibility, does not mention the v2 upgrade, and the new resolver it builds will depend on this hook. If pydantic-ai is upgraded to v2 concurrently or soon after this ticket lands, the assertion may be stale.

findings.finding: `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` is described as already existing ('which exists for exactly this') as the escape hatch for fallback chains, but it does not exist anywhere in src/ or docs/. The plan frames it as a present-tense mechanism that operators can rely on today, but no code in the repo reads or documents this env var.
findings.location: Approach section — 'fallback is deliberately CONFIG-FILE-ONLY… An environment needing a fallback chain uses `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` (the sibling ticket), which exists for exactly this.'
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'which exists for exactly this' to 'which the sibling ticket will provide' and add a `[rebar:<ticket-id>]` citation so the prerequisite relationship is explicit and auditable.

findings.finding: The `fallback` array is described as 'an array of sub-objects' that is 'PARSED and carried' but the sub-object schema (its fields, types, and required vs. optional status) is never defined anywhere in the plan or in existing code. An implementor has no spec to write the parser or the AC test against.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Each slot accepts `model`, `provider`, `endpoint`, and an optional `fallback` array; the array is PARSED and carried now' / Testing section: 'a `fallback` array parses and is carried on the record without being consumed'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'Each `fallback` entry is a mapping with the same fields as the parent slot (`model`, `provider`, `endpoint`); `model` is required in every entry, `provider` and `endpoint` are optional and resolve identically to top-level slot fields. A missing-`model` entry in the array is a config error.'

findings.finding: The `fallback` array sub-object schema is described only as 'an array of sub-objects' with no field specification — an executor building a dataclass or Pydantic model cannot know whether sub-objects carry the same fields as the parent slot (model, provider, endpoint) or a different shape.
findings.location: Approach section — 'fallback array' paragraph; Testing bullet — 'a fallback array parses and is carried on the record'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'Each entry in the `fallback` array carries the same optional fields as the parent slot (`model`, `provider`, `endpoint`) — no additional fields are permitted, and `api_key` is rejected by the same rule as the parent.'

findings.finding: AC7 requires `docs/env-vars.md` to regenerate with no diff, but the Approach section introduces six new env vars (REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL, REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_PROVIDER, REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_ENDPOINT, and STANDARD_/TRIVIAL_ equivalents) that would appear in the generated output — causing a diff unless the doc is also updated. Yet the Scope section names only `src/rebar/llm/config.py` and `tests/unit/` as deliverables, with no mention of updating `docs/env-vars.md`. This is a cross-section contradiction: Scope says no doc file is touched, AC7 implies it must be current (and the Approach guarantees new content exists to add).
findings.location: Scope section vs. Acceptance Criteria AC7 vs. Approach (env-var naming section)
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope section, add: '- `docs/env-vars.md` — regenerate (or update the generator's source registry) to include the six new REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_*/STANDARD_*/TRIVIAL_* env vars; AC7 verifies no remaining drift.' This removes the contradiction and makes the drift-gate a meaningful post-implementation check rather than a surprising failure.

findings.finding: AC7 asserts `docs/env-vars.md` regenerates with no diff, but the plan introduces six new env vars (`REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL`, `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_PROVIDER`, `REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_ENDPOINT`, and `STANDARD_`/`TRIVIAL_` variants) that `gen_env_registry.py` will auto-discover via `_llm_str` calls (listed in `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`). A no-diff outcome is impossible unless the new vars are explicitly excluded from the scanner, which the plan does not specify.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC7: '`docs/env-vars.md` regenerates with no diff (the generator is drift-gated)'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace AC7 with: '`docs/env-vars.md` is regenerated to include `REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_{MODEL,PROVIDER,ENDPOINT}` and the CI drift gate (`python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check`) exits 0 on the committed result.'
